newsitem.title: GERMANY: Kirch son says German local TV still weak.
newsitem.headline: Kirch son says German local TV still weak.

text.p: Developing local, advertising-financed television remains difficult, German media investor Thomas Kirch, son of television and film mogul Leo Kirch, said in an interview with the ProSieben Media AG in-house newsletter CineChart published on Friday.

"There still aren't any real local TV advertising markets that have developed (in Germany)," Kirch, who is a majority shareholder in ProSieben Media AG, told CineChart. "The production of local TV advertising is still too costly."
He said that supplying programming for a local station, however, proved relatively simple in larger cities.
"Cities like Hamburg, Berlin and Munich, in which there is something happening 24 hours a day, provide enough material for an interesting local new programme," Kirch said.
He added that there was also a wealth of series and films which the large networks do not use but would still draw an audience which local stations ought to take advantage of.

The recent bankruptcy of Berlin local station Puls-TV, which had counted Central European Media Enterprises and Time-Warner Entertainment among its investors, sent ripples of doubt about the future of German local TV through the industry.
Media experts have speculated that Thomas Kirch will buy Puls-TV. He did not address plans for the station in the interview.
